title: What's Next: AL-Go for GitHub (2025 release wave 1)

chapters.title: Moving Away from BC Container Helper

features.name: Indirect Templates and Customizations
features.description: Allows partners to create indirect or private templates for repositories to enable customer-specific customizations without modifying final repositories. The feature will merge custom jobs and custom steps into templates.
caveats: Currently in PR stage being tested by partners

features.name: NuGet Support - Generate and Publish Runtime Packages
features.description: Enable efficient generation and publishing of runtime packages as NuGet, addressing a frequently heard partner request for an efficient way to share apps.
caveats: Requires more testing and adoption across partners

features.name: Running Tests on Online Environments
features.description: Ability to run tests and page scripting tests on online environments when publishing to sandbox or QA environments, integrated as part of the publishing effort.
features.status_evidence_quote: in this release we have released a functionality that can publish test and test apps and stuff like that to online environments
caveats: Page scripting tests as part of publishing, not core CI/CD pipeline

features.name: Move Away from BC Container Helper
features.description: AL-Go for GitHub will transition away from using BC Container Helper and move DevOps-relevant features into PowerShell modules or GitHub actions. The process is expected to take two to three years.
caveats: Partners managing own DevOps will need to migrate
BC Container Helper will remain in PowerShell gallery during transition

features.name: Security Recommendations Implementation
features.description: AL-Go for GitHub will benefit from Microsoft's security investments and provide a secure and reliable platform. Monthly security updates from Microsoft teams are implemented in DevOps pipelines.
